stem: When his father Maha Singh died in 1792, the twelve-year-old Ranjit Singh became chief of which misl?
options: the Bhangi misl
the Kanhaiya misl
the Sukerchakia misl
the Faizullapuria misl
why: Ranjit Singh's grandfather Charat Singh and father Maha Singh led the Sukerchakia misl, based at Gujranwala; Ranjit Singh inherited it as a boy and built the kingdom from it. The Kanhaiya misl, led by his mother-in-law Sada Kaur, was an ally, not his inheritance.
source: Sikh histories of the misl period; Sukerchakia misl, Gujranwala

es.stem: Cuando murió su padre, Maha Singh, en 1792, Ranjit Singh, con doce años, quedó como jefe de ¿qué misl?
options: el misl Bhangi
el misl Kanhaiya
el misl Sukerchakia
el misl Faizullapuria
es.why: El abuelo de Ranjit Singh, Charat Singh, y su padre, Maha Singh, dirigieron el misl Sukerchakia, con base en Gujranwala; Ranjit Singh lo heredó de niño y construyó el reino a partir de él. El misl Kanhaiya, dirigido por su suegra Sada Kaur, fue un aliado, no su herencia.

stem: In the misl period, the Sarbat Khalsa met at Amritsar, usually at Vaisakhi and Diwali, and made decisions before the Guru Granth Sahib that bound every band. What was such a decision called?
options: a gurmata
a rehitnama
a janamsakhi
a dharamsal
why: A gurmata (literally "the Guru's counsel") was a resolution adopted by the gathered Khalsa in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib, at the Akal Takht; it bound all the misls. A rehitnama is a manual of conduct, a janamsakhi a life story of Guru Nanak, and a dharamsal an early place of worship.
source: Sarbat Khalsa and gurmata at the Akal Takht, 18th century

es.stem: En la época de los misls, el Sarbat Khalsa se reunía en Amritsar, por lo general en Vaisakhi y Diwali, y tomaba decisiones ante el Guru Granth Sahib que obligaban a todas las bandas. ¿Cómo se llamaba una decisión así?
options: un gurmata
un rehitnama
un janamsakhi
un dharamsal
es.why: Un gurmata (literalmente "el consejo del Gurú") era una resolución que adoptaba el Khalsa reunido en presencia del Guru Granth Sahib, en el Akal Takht; obligaba a todos los misls. Un rehitnama es un manual de conducta, un janamsakhi un relato de la vida de Guru Nanak y un dharamsal un antiguo lugar de culto.

stem: Maharaja Ranjit Singh ruled Punjab as the Sarkar-e-Khalsa, yet his Nanakshahi coins left off his own name. What did their Persian verse do in its place?
options: named the Mughal emperor in Delhi as the true sovereign
listed the misl chiefs who shared the rule of Punjab
recorded his treaty of friendship with the British
gave the victory to Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh
why: Ranjit Singh's Nanakshahi coins carried a Persian couplet ("Degh o tegh o fateh...") saying the bounty, the sword and the victory came from Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh, as earlier Sikh coins and seals had. Sarkar-e-Khalsa means "the government of the Khalsa": the rule was presented as the Gurus' gift, not the king's own.
source: Nanakshahi coinage of Ranjit Singh (Degh Tegh Fateh couplet); Sarkar-e-Khalsa

es.stem: El Maharaja Ranjit Singh gobernó el Panyab como el Sarkar-e-Khalsa, pero sus monedas nanakshahi no llevaban su propio nombre. ¿Qué hacía en su lugar su verso persa?
options: nombraba al emperador mogol de Delhi como el verdadero soberano
enumeraba a los jefes de misl que compartían el gobierno del Panyab
registraba su tratado de amistad con los británicos
daba la victoria a Guru Nanak y a Guru Gobind Singh
es.why: Las monedas nanakshahi de Ranjit Singh llevaban un pareado persa ("Degh o tegh o fateh...") que decía que la abundancia, la espada y la victoria venían de Guru Nanak y de Guru Gobind Singh, como antes lo habían hecho monedas y sellos sijs. Sarkar-e-Khalsa significa "el gobierno del Khalsa": el gobierno se presentaba como don de los Gurús, no como propiedad del rey.

stem: Sikh tradition says Akali Phula Singh, serving at the Akal Takht, summoned Maharaja Ranjit Singh for a breach of Sikh discipline, and the Maharaja came and accepted his penance. What does the story show?
options: the Maharaja could appoint and dismiss the Akal Takht's leaders
even the ruler was answerable to the Khalsa at the Akal Takht
the Akal Takht dealt only with war and land, never with conduct
a penance at the Akal Takht could be bought off with a gift of land
why: The Akal Takht, raised by Guru Hargobind, is the seat from which the Khalsa calls any Sikh to account. In the common telling, Ranjit Singh came barefoot with folded hands and accepted the tankhah (penance), showing that the ruler, too, stood under the Panth's discipline.
source: Akal Takht; tradition of Akali Phula Singh and Ranjit Singh

es.stem: La tradición sij cuenta que Akali Phula Singh, que servía en el Akal Takht, llamó al Maharaja Ranjit Singh por faltar a la disciplina sij, y que el Maharaja acudió y aceptó su penitencia. ¿Qué muestra el relato?
options: el Maharaja podía nombrar y destituir a los líderes del Akal Takht
aun el gobernante respondía ante el Khalsa en el Akal Takht
el Akal Takht trataba solo de guerra y tierras, nunca de conducta
una penitencia del Akal Takht se podía saldar con un regalo de tierras
es.why: El Akal Takht, levantado por Guru Hargobind, es la sede desde la que el Khalsa pide cuentas a cualquier sij. En la versión más común, Ranjit Singh llegó descalzo y con las manos juntas y aceptó la tankhah (penitencia), lo que muestra que también el gobernante estaba bajo la disciplina del Panth.

stem: In a salok in the Guru Granth Sahib (Ang 787, Var Suhi), Guru Amar Das says that women who burn on their husband's pyre are not true satis. Who does he say is truly called a sati?
options: a woman who burns with her husband to prove her loyalty
a woman who lives in virtue and contentment, serving God
a woman who leaves her home to wander as a renunciant
a woman who keeps a vow of silence for the rest of her life
why: Ang 787: "they are not called satis who burn themselves with the corpses"; true satis are those who live in good conduct and contentment, serving the Lord and remembering him every day. The Gurus rejected the burning of widows, which is why the satis at Ranjit Singh's funeral in 1839 are remembered with sorrow.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 787 (Var Suhi, salok of Guru Amar Das)

es.stem: En un salok del Guru Granth Sahib (Ang 787, Var Suhi), Guru Amar Das dice que las mujeres que se queman en la pira de su esposo no son verdaderas satis. ¿A quién llama él de verdad sati?
options: a la mujer que arde con su esposo para probar su lealtad
a la que vive con bondad y contento, sirviendo al Señor
a la mujer que deja su casa para vagar como renunciante
a la que guarda un voto de silencio por el resto de su vida
es.why: Ang 787: "no se llaman satis las que se queman con los cadáveres"; las verdaderas satis son las que viven con buena conducta y contento, sirviendo al Señor y recordándolo cada día. Los Gurús rechazaron la quema de viudas, por eso las satis del funeral de Ranjit Singh en 1839 se recuerdan con tristeza.

stem: A traveller in an unfamiliar town sees a tall pole wrapped in saffron cloth, flying a triangular saffron flag with the Khanda emblem. Going by the Sikh Rehat Maryada, what does it tell her?
options: a Sikh family nearby is mourning a death
a Sikh regiment is stationed in the town
a gurdwara is here, open to all who come
a Gurpurab fair will be held here this week
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada says every gurdwara should fly a Nishan Sahib on a tall pole; it marks the gurdwara, where anyone may enter, share langar and find shelter. In the misl era the Nishanwalia misl carried the Khalsa's standard in battle.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, chapter on gurdwaras (Nishan Sahib)

es.stem: Una viajera, en un pueblo que no conoce, ve un poste alto envuelto en tela azafrán, con una bandera triangular azafrán que lleva el emblema del Khanda. Según el Sikh Rehat Maryada, ¿qué le indica?
options: una familia sij cercana está de luto por una muerte
un regimiento sij está acuartelado en el pueblo
aquí hay un gurdwara, abierto a todos
esta semana habrá aquí una feria de Gurpurab
es.why: El Sikh Rehat Maryada dice que todo gurdwara debe tener un Nishan Sahib en un poste alto; señala el gurdwara, donde cualquiera puede entrar, compartir el langar y encontrar refugio. En la época de los misls, el misl Nishanwalia llevaba el estandarte del Khalsa en batalla.

stem: In 1886 Maharaja Duleep Singh, Ranjit Singh's youngest son, set out from Britain for India. What happened on that journey, and why is it remembered by Sikhs?
why: The British, not wanting him in India, stopped him at Aden. There he took amrit, the Khalsa initiation, returning to the faith of his father after being baptized a Christian as a boy. He never reached the Punjab and died in Paris in 1893.
source: Life of Maharaja Duleep Singh; Aden, 1886

rubric.point: Says the British stopped or detained him on the way, at Aden, so he did not reach India. Saying only that 'he never got there' without the British stopping him counts as partly.
Says he took amrit (the Khalsa initiation) there, returning to Sikhi. Saying only that he 'became religious' does not count.
Mentions that he had been baptized a Christian as a boy, or that he died in exile in Paris (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En 1886, el Maharaja Duleep Singh, el hijo menor de Ranjit Singh, partió de Gran Bretaña hacia la India. ¿Qué pasó en ese viaje y por qué lo recuerdan los sijs?
es.why: Los británicos, que no lo querían en la India, lo detuvieron en Adén. Allí tomó amrit, la iniciación del Khalsa, y volvió a la fe de su padre después de haber sido bautizado cristiano de niño. Nunca llegó al Punyab y murió en París en 1893.

stem: After the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46), how did Kashmir pass out of the Sikh kingdom of Lahore, and to whom?
why: Under the Treaty of Lahore (1846) the kingdom owed the British a war indemnity it could not pay, so it ceded Kashmir and the hill country instead. A week later, by the Treaty of Amritsar, the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra raja of Jammu, who had served at Ranjit Singh's court.
source: Treaties of Lahore and Amritsar, March 1846

rubric.point: Says Lahore ceded Kashmir to the British in place of a war payment (indemnity) it could not meet. Saying only 'the British took it in the war' counts as partly.
Says the British then sold or transferred it to Gulab Singh, the Dogra raja of Jammu. Naming 'a Dogra ruler' without Gulab Singh counts as partly.
Names the treaties of Lahore and Amritsar, or notes that Gulab Singh had served Ranjit Singh's court (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Después de la Primera Guerra Anglo-Sij (1845-46), ¿cómo salió Cachemira del reino sij de Lahore, y a manos de quién pasó?
es.why: Por el Tratado de Lahore (1846), el reino debía a los británicos una indemnización de guerra que no podía pagar, así que en su lugar cedió Cachemira y las tierras de las colinas. Una semana después, por el Tratado de Amritsar, los británicos vendieron Cachemira a Gulab Singh, el raja dogra de Jammu, que había servido en la corte de Ranjit Singh.
